title: doctor_deadline tests start their 5 s diagnostic deadline before two PowerShell startups, so under load they fail after 60 s waits
outcome: The doctor_deadline tests measure only the doctor's deadline behaviour, not PowerShell startup latency. Their readiness phase can't be starved by a deadline that started before the fixture was ready, and a failure prints the worker's real error.
acceptance: The diagnostic deadline under test starts only after the fixture's descendant-ready and process-probe handshake completes (or the test otherwise excludes fixture startup from the measured budget), without increasing any timeout value; a test or deterministic hook shows that a slow fixture startup no longer causes the deadline to kill the doctor before the handshake.
When the readiness phase fails, the test output includes the worker's actual error (not only 'timed out waiting on channel'), covered by a test of the failure path.
Both doctor_deadline tests pass in a full five-stage gate on the exact final input, and an independent review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.

completion.summary: The doctor_deadline readiness/probe handshake is excluded from its diagnostic deadline, readiness failures preserve the worker error, and the exact integrated input passed the five-stage full gate with a clean worktree. Independent evaluation f9aa3e8b6eb047fd968c32ed2b185b03 passed all three criteria.
